primary_sources.title: Baer and Ballmann, Guide to Boundary Value Problems for Dirac-Type Operators, v1
primary_sources.reviewed: Theorems 3.9 and 3.11 on boundary regularity and self-adjointness; Corollary 3.17 on local elliptic boundary conditions.
primary_sources.use: Regularity on the smooth half-domain with the actual paired local elliptic projector. Uniformity in the moving cut is derived by the explicit smooth common-domain pullback; no smooth-double theorem is invoked.

source_access: Primary PDF opened directly and the stated results read; no downloaded-byte digest claimed.
strongest_comparator: The retained geodesic-seam comparison already controls global attachment at zero cut but does not give a moving-domain limit. The preceding chart-contact theorem does not include the two-vertex row sum.
hardest_step: Keep the actual paired domain fixed by a smooth half-domain pullback, derive uniform separated trace-ideal bounds on a complex mass circle, and retain the mass derivative in the diagonal constant probe.
new_consequence: The separated and actual-to-cap global massive quadratic response, including its diagonal partners, has an ordinary moving-cut limit at the fixed Euclidean seed. The unresolved quantum comparison is local to the curved moving boundary and its ultraviolet contacts.
remaining_quantum_gap: The local curved finite-cut cap Hessian minus the normal representative remains unproved. Its near-diagonal and reflected kernels, local contacts, and all local shape partners must be combined before any branch exclusion.
regulator_contract: Retain the original exponential chart, paired domain, fixed Euclidean period and spin structure, angular tower, common subtraction and finite coefficients. Auxiliary caps are analytic comparison tools, not replacement physical states.
verification_scope: Finite skew-adjoint matrix families independently test locality, both vertices, row sums, mass derivatives and moving-operator continuity; exact counting identities and bounded angular sums test the summable envelope. These are diagnostics supporting the ordinary argument, not actual charged-kernel evaluations.
initial_diagnostic_failure: The first frozen run incorrectly imposed [A,chi]chi=chi[A,chi] on finite matrices. This multiplication identity holds for the continuum first-order differential operator, but not for the finite diagnostic. Retain the exact finite-matrix correction xi B[[A,chi],chi]B xi/2 and test the continuum identity separately. Failed sources and run are preserved.
